headline: Shopify is opening its catalog of more than a billion product listings to more AI shopping agents, but buyers must approve each purchase.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a large e-commerce platform widens agent shopping to any agent, but it is an extension of an earlier Meta deal with approval still required.
importance_line: Online shoppers will be able to hand buying tasks to the AI agent they choose, within budget and shipping rules, but it sits inside a wider fight, including Amazon against Perplexity and Meta's Muse, over whether agents may shop for customers.
summary: The Verge reports that Shopify announced on Tuesday that shoppers will be able to link their own AI agent to their account on the Shop app and have it browse and buy from a catalog of more than a billion listings, with one-click checkout through Shop Pay and approval needed for every purchase. It widens a September deal that let Meta's Muse agent shop on Shopify, because any agent can now be used without a partnership.
notes: Read in full on The Verge. The article says more agents "will soon" be able to shop, so the exact start date is not given.
